svg.title: Pulsus Dash — Multi-cloud estate as a 3D world (Atlas Map, INC-2041)
svg.desc: Atlas Map view in Orbit after flying down from the globe: a perspective 3D world of a hybrid multi-cloud estate. Each provider (AWS, AZURE, GCP, OCI, ON-PREM, OPENSTACK) is an outlined neutral island named only by a monochrome text badge, never vendor colours or logos. Regions and the lon-dc1 data centre are plateaus; accounts, subscriptions, projects and compartments are dashed fenced lots. One shape per class family: buildings for compute and Kubernetes districts (EKS, AKS, GKE, OpenShift), cylinders for databases, squat cylinders for caches, flat ribbons for queues and streams, grid-topped vault slabs for object storage, floating cube swarms for functions, arch gates for load balancers, rack slabs for network devices. Managed services carry a managed badge; self-hosted pg-legacy is the same cylinder without it. Hybrid links are bridges: VPN to lon-dc1, Interconnect from gcp, and a Watch-state azure-aws peering. INC-2041 overlay: aws eu-west-1 Degraded since 12:22 after the 12:19 timeout change, checkout district and its load balancer are victims with dashed rings, probable origin psp-api stands outside the estate under a beacon, about 38k euro per hour at risk. An unknown aws::AppRunner::Service is a hatched generic box. Estate strip with class and provider totals and coverage; docked 2D health matrix by provider and class; shape-grammar legend; six callouts.
